newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares scale new highs, run not yet over.
newsitem.headline: German shares scale new highs, run not yet over.

text.p: Following the German share market's race to yet another record level on Friday, dealers predict the market will remain at high levels next week, still underpinned by talk of consolidation in the banking sector.

The 30-share blue chip DAX index closed up over one percent or up 42.44 points at 3,604.55 on Friday but gave up some ground on profit-taking in electronic IBIS trading in late afternoon as Wall Street opened with losses.
Despite the move, dealers remain convinced there is still more room for the DAX to climb. "The DAX can still climb further," a dealer said.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan to gain access to a significantly larger Bundesbank profit by first unlocking some hidden Bundesbank reserves is seen to smack of the accounting irregularities Germany had until now abhorred.

"This just opens the door for currency union with more members," said Joachim Fels, econoimst at Morgan Stanley in London, adding that such speculation would likely drive the dollar even higher in the future.
A higher dollar also is seen to benefit the share market, particularly as Germany's economy is driven largely by exports.
At the same time signs of a further consolidation in the banking sector, were also seen to underpin the market.
BHF Bank and Bankgesellschaft Berlin both rose amid speculation that Bankgesellschaft, fresh from announcing it was in merger talks with a regional bank, would make a play for BHF Bank.
The shares gave up some gains when each side denied the talk, but analysts still said there might be some gains in store for other banking shares in light of the consolidation talk.
Although Friday was expected to be a slow day devoid of record-breaking activity as dealers eyed a three day weekend, a number of factors came together to boost the index.
Wall Street's strong performance overnight helped buoy the market early in the session as did the dollar's jump over the 1.70 level.

Analysts argued that part of the dollar's strength could be attributed to uncertainty about Europe's planned currency union which was seen notching up in light of Germany's ill-timed announcement on plans to revalue gold stocks.
The market will be closed on Monday and regular trading resumes on Tuesday.
